evals.prompt: Can you review PR #212 before I merge it? The diff is in mcp_ticket_server.diff — it's a new MCP server for our helpdesk that people will plug into Claude Desktop. Tell me what needs to change.
evals.expected_output: A Backend / API / MCP review using the template that catches the stdio stdout corruption from print(), the api_key tool parameter (and README telling users to paste the key into chat), the readOnlyHint lie on get_ticket that assigns + marks read, the ticket_action mega-tool with polymorphic params and inconsistent keys, path traversal in read_attachment, the unbounded list_tickets output, opaque/unrecoverable errors, and the unguarded hard delete.
expectations: Flags that print() writes to stdout in a stdio MCP server, which corrupts the JSON-RPC protocol stream (logs must go to stderr)
Flags api_key as a tool parameter (secret passed through the model/transcript) and says credentials should come from the server's environment/config instead
Flags that get_ticket is annotated readOnlyHint=True but has side effects (assigns the ticket and/or marks it read)
Flags the ticket_action tool design: free-string action plus untyped/polymorphic params dict with a vague description, recommending separate typed tools or an enum/discriminated schema
Flags path traversal in read_attachment: os.path.join with an unvalidated path can escape ATTACHMENT_ROOT (absolute path or ../)
Flags that list_tickets returns an unbounded result (per_page=100000, no pagination/cap/truncation) into the model's context
Flags that errors are not recoverable for the model (e.g. 'Error: 404' strings, raw raise_for_status/ValueError) and recommends isError results with what/why/next-step guidance
Flags delete_ticket as a destructive hard delete with no confirmation, dry-run, or destructiveHint annotation
Flags that the write actions (comment / escalate / merge) are not idempotent, so a model or client retry after a timeout posts duplicates
Flags that HELPDESK_URL silently falls back to a hard-coded production URL when the env var is missing (should fail fast at startup)
Flags that ticket_id / params values are interpolated unescaped into the Helpdesk API path, so '../' can reach other API routes
Uses the review template: output contains 'Backend / API / MCP Reviewer' and a Model field identifying the reviewing model

evals.prompt: Review this orders API change before we merge — it's in orders_api.diff. Heads up, this is our public v1 API that the mobile apps and a bunch of partners use.
evals.expected_output: A Backend / API / MCP review that catches the breaking v1 response changes (total → totalCents, created_at → createdAt, public_id → internal bigint id), 200 + success:false, missing Idempotency-Key on refund, money as float, leaking err.stack, unbounded page_size + bare array + arbitrary sort, the side-effecting GET, and OpenAPI drift (spec says 201 / dollars).
expectations: Flags the breaking change to the published v1 order response (total removed/renamed to totalCents and/or created_at renamed to createdAt) and recommends keeping the old field / versioning / deprecation instead of changing v1 in place
Flags that the order id switched from public_id to the internal id as a breaking change (and/or notes IDs should be strings / not internal auto-increment)
Flags returning HTTP 200 with {success:false} for failures instead of proper 4xx status codes
Flags that the refund POST has no Idempotency-Key (or equivalent), so a client retry can issue a duplicate refund
Flags money handled as a float (parseFloat dollars / amount * 100 / float amount stored)
Flags the 500 error response leaking err.stack / internal error messages
Flags that page_size is not clamped to a server-side maximum (unbounded page size)
Flags that the sort parameter is not allowlisted (clients can sort by arbitrary columns)
Flags that the list endpoint returns a bare JSON array with no envelope / pagination metadata
Flags the GET /v1/orders/:id handler writing to the database (touchLastViewed) as a side-effecting GET
Flags OpenAPI drift on the refund endpoint: the spec documents 201 but the handler returns 200
Flags that the OpenAPI spec was not updated for the changed order response (totalCents/createdAt/id) and/or documents amount as dollars-as-number
Rates the refund authorization gap (any authenticated user of the account can issue refunds; no role/permission check) at Major or higher, rather than only deferring it to another reviewer
Rates customer_email newly exposed in every order response (PII) at Major or higher, rather than only deferring it to another reviewer
Flags that the refund cap is not cumulative (previous refunds are not counted) and/or not protected against concurrent refunds, so total refunds can exceed the order total
Flags that the provider refund is executed before any local record is written, so a failed insert or crash leaves money moved with no record and a retry refunds again

[breadth] Flags that total_cents may be missing/NULL for existing orders (no backfill in the diff) and that this breaks the over-refund guard (it either rejects legitimate refunds or lets any amount through)
Uses the review template: output contains 'Backend / API / MCP Reviewer' and a Model field identifying the reviewing model

evals.prompt: we're about to ship a hosted MCP server for billing so our support agent and claude.ai can look up invoices and issue refunds. diff is remote_billing_mcp.diff. give it a proper review before it goes live
evals.expected_output: A Backend / API / MCP review that catches token passthrough to the provider, no audience validation on the JWT, session id used as authentication (and predictable session ids), no Origin validation / cors *, provider call inside the DB transaction with no idempotency key while annotated idempotentHint, the arbitrary SQL tool, unbounded export_invoices, and the webhook with no signature check and no event-id dedupe.
expectations: Flags token passthrough: the user's SSO/Okta token is forwarded to the payment provider API, which the MCP spec forbids (server should use its own credentials for downstream calls)
Flags that jwt.verify does not validate the token audience/resource, so any Okta-signed token for any app is accepted
Flags that an existing Mcp-Session-Id is treated as proof of authentication (requests with a known session skip auth) and/or that session ids are predictable (sub + Date.now())
Flags missing Origin header validation (cors origin '*', no Origin check) on the Streamable HTTP endpoint
Flags that issue_refund calls the provider over the network inside the DB transaction (locks held across a remote call; provider success + rollback leaves money moved with no record)
Flags that issue_refund is not idempotent (no idempotency key to the provider / retries double-refund) and that idempotentHint: true is therefore false
Flags run_billing_query as an arbitrary-SQL tool exposed to an agent (prompt-injection reachable, not read-only enforced)
Flags export_invoices returning an unbounded result (40k+ rows) into the model context without pagination/cap
Flags the provider webhook: no signature verification and/or no dedupe on event id, so redelivery double-credits the customer
Rates the missing per-account/tenant authorization on the billing tools (get_invoice / issue_refund / export_invoices act on any id) at Major or higher, rather than only deferring it
Flags the refund state inconsistency: refundedCents is updated at request time while ledger/balance change only on the webhook, and provider failure / refund.failed is never reconciled
[breadth] Flags that the provider webhook can arrive before issue_refund's DB transaction commits (refund row not yet visible), so settlement fails or matches the wrong refund
Uses the review template: output contains 'Backend / API / MCP Reviewer' and a Model field identifying the reviewing model

evals.prompt: Please review PR #903 (expense_mcp_v2.diff). It moves our expenses MCP server to the new SDK v2 and adds PIN confirmation for approvals. Finance wants it live next week.
evals.expected_output: Catches spec/SDK-dependent defects: PIN collected via form-mode elicitation (spec requires URL mode for credentials), bind_principal=None + approving as the approver_id from request state instead of the verified caller, hard-coded fallback request-state key, public cacheScope on a role-filtered tools/list, v2 SDK hiding non-ToolError exception text from the model, breaking tool rename, removed pagination with inline receipt images, 0.0.0.0 bind disabling Host/Origin checks, and reimburse without idempotency.
expectations: Flags that the approval PIN is collected via form-mode elicitation, which the MCP spec forbids for passwords/credentials (must use URL-mode elicitation)

Flags that approval identity comes from request state rather than the verified caller: bind_principal=None leaves sealed state unbound to the user and/or approve() never checks current_user() is the expense's approver
Flags the hard-coded fallback REQUEST_STATE_KEY ('expenses-dev-request-state-key') used when the env var is missing (forgeable state; should fail at startup)
Flags cache_hints scope='public' on tools/list even though the tool list is filtered by role (must be 'private'), so one user's tool list can be served to another

Flags that raising ValueError/RuntimeError/PermissionError in SDK v2 gives the model only a generic 'Error executing tool' message, so expected failures should raise ToolError (or return isError) with recovery guidance
Flags the tool rename (list_pending_expenses/approve_expense -> dotted names) with the old names removed as a breaking change for existing clients/agent workflows, recommending aliases/deprecation
Flags that expenses.list_pending lost the v1 cursor pagination and 50-item cap (default 200, no max) and inlines receipt images, blowing up the model's context
Flags that host='0.0.0.0' with transport_security=None leaves the SDK's Host/Origin (DNS-rebinding) validation disabled
Flags that expenses.reimburse moves money with no idempotency key/guard, so a retry can schedule a duplicate payout
[breadth] Flags that expenses.reimburse is protected only by hiding it from the role-filtered tool list, with no authorization check inside the handler
Uses the review template: output contains 'Backend / API / MCP Reviewer' and a Model field identifying the reviewing model

evals.prompt: review payments_api_v2.diff please. adds idempotency keys, cursor pagination and If-Match to our public v2 payments API. tests are green, want to merge today
evals.expected_output: Catches subtle contract/semantics defects inside features that look implemented: racy check-then-act idempotency stored after the side effect, key not scoped per merchant, no request fingerprint; cursor on non-unique created_at skipping rows; page->cursor switch breaking v2 clients; second-resolution ETag and non-atomic If-Match; merge-patch null not clearing fields; new enum value breaking closed-enum clients.
expectations: Flags the idempotency check-then-act race: two concurrent requests with the same key both miss the cache and both charge (needs an atomic reservation such as SET NX / unique insert before calling the PSP)
Flags that the idempotency record is written only after the PSP charge, so a crash/timeout between the charge and the redis.set lets a retry charge again
Flags that the idempotency key is not scoped to the merchant (idem:{key} is global), so one merchant's key can return another merchant's charge
Flags that a reused key with a different request body silently returns the original response instead of rejecting it (no request fingerprint)
Flags that the cursor uses only created_at with a strict '<', so invoices sharing a timestamp at a page boundary are skipped (needs a unique tiebreaker such as (created_at, id))
Flags that replacing page/page_size with cursor is a breaking change for existing v2 clients (old params are silently ignored)
Flags that the ETag is derived from updated_at truncated to whole seconds, so two updates in the same second share an ETag and If-Match cannot detect the conflict
Flags that the If-Match comparison and the save are not atomic (read-check-write race), so concurrent PATCHes can still lose updates (needs a conditional UPDATE)
Flags that PATCH ignores null values, so clients cannot clear a field, contradicting the JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) semantics the PR promises
Flags that adding the partially_paid enum value is a breaking change for existing clients/SDKs that decode status as a closed enum
[breadth] Flags that db.invoices.save() writes the whole invoice object, so a concurrent change to other fields (e.g. status/amount from a payment webhook) is overwritten
Uses the review template: output contains 'Backend / API / MCP Reviewer' and a Model field identifying the reviewing model

evals.prompt: Can you review usage_credits_outbox.diff (PR #340)? It's the outbox + credits consumer work for billing.
evals.expected_output: Catches at-least-once semantics defects: relay marks published before sending (loss) and has no row claiming across 3 replicas (duplicates); consumer commits the dedupe marker outside any transaction with the debit (lost debit on failure); read-modify-write credit debit (lost updates); email retry of a non-idempotent POST and swallowed failures; low-balance email on every event; cache invalidated before commit; visibility timeout shorter than worst-case processing.
expectations: Flags that the relay sets published_at before sending to SQS, so a failed send loses the event permanently
Flags that the relay does not claim/lock rows (e.g. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), so its 3 replicas publish the same events concurrently

Flags that the processed_events marker is committed separately from (before) the credit debit with no enclosing transaction, so a failure after the insert makes the redelivered message be skipped and the debit is lost
Flags that the credit debit is a read-modify-write of an absolute value, so concurrent events for the same account lose debits (needs an atomic credits = credits - units)
Flags that send_email_with_retry retries a non-idempotent POST on timeout without an idempotency key (duplicate emails) and/or treats HTTP error responses as success / swallows final failure
Flags that the low-balance email is sent on every event while below the threshold rather than once when the threshold is crossed
Flags that change_plan deletes the cache key inside the transaction before commit, so a concurrent get_plan can re-cache the old plan for the TTL
Flags that the 30s SQS visibility timeout is shorter than the worst-case time to process a batch (sequential handling + email retries/backoff), causing redelivery while still processing
[breadth] Flags that negative or otherwise invalid event units would add credits (no validation of units before the debit)
[breadth] Flags that one failing outbox row (unknown topic KeyError, send error) blocks the relay from progressing past it (no skip / dead-letter)
Uses the review template: output contains 'Backend / API / MCP Reviewer' and a Model field identifying the reviewing model

evals.prompt: can you review PR #77 (inventory_fulfillment.diff) before we ship it? it's the reservations + carrier tracking work for checkout
evals.expected_output: HELD-OUT (written after round-3 skill edits; not used to design them). Catches: unvalidated/negative quantity increasing stock; whole-row product save clobbering concurrent stock changes; toISOString on NULL carrier_eta 500ing every existing order; out-of-order carrier events regressing status; non-idempotent returned restock / duplicate order.delivered; unhandled unknown event type or tracking number; reservations never released; missing estimatedDelivery wiping stored ETA.
expectations: Flags that quantity is not validated: a negative (or zero/non-integer/non-numeric) quantity passes the stock check and a negative value increases stock
Flags that PUT /v1/products/:id saves the entire product row (including stock), so stock changes made concurrently by reservations are overwritten
Flags that estimatedDelivery calls toISOString() on carrier_eta, which is NULL for all existing orders (new nullable column, no backfill), so GET /v1/orders/:id returns 500 for existing orders
Flags that carrier events can arrive out of order (e.g. in_transit after delivered) and the consumer regresses order status with no state-transition guard
Flags that the carrier consumer is not idempotent: a redelivered shipment.returned restocks twice and/or order.delivered is published more than once
Flags that an unknown event type (status undefined) or an unknown tracking number (order not found) is not handled, leading to a bad write or a thrown error and repeated redelivery
Flags that expired reservations are never released (nothing returns stock after the 15-minute hold)
Flags that an event without estimatedDelivery overwrites an existing carrier_eta with null
Uses the review template: output contains 'Backend / API / MCP Reviewer' and a Model field identifying the reviewing model
